messages:
Maria Chen: FYI AcmeCorp follow-up: they accepted the initial answers but want a verifiable, redacted SIEM export + a tiny audit trace that proves support sessions are ephemeral. Can we produce a single package (redacted logs + verification steps + short explainer)?

Kevin O'Neill: I can build the package. Quick constraints: no real tenant IDs, no PII, and sample must be verifiable by them (HMAC or signature). Prefer HMAC with a one-off verification key.

Priya Desai: We should also include a note explaining how KMS calls are proxied so support never unwraps customer KEKs. That was a sticking point in the call.

Daniel Ruiz: I'll pull the session lifecycle logs. We'll redact tenant_id, swap with <TENANT_REDACTED>, and include session lifecycle lines: create, authorize, revoke/expire. Short and machine-parseable.

Maria Chen: Good. Keep each log single-line JSON. They asked for newline-delimited JSON examples (ndjson).

Kevin O'Neill: Draft ndjson sample below (redacted):

```json
{"ts":"2026-03-02T09:12:01Z","svc":"auth","evt":"session.create","actor":"support:priyad","session":"s-abc123","tenant":"<TENANT_REDACTED>","ttl":1800}
{"ts":"2026-03-02T09:12:05Z","svc":"auth","evt":"session.authorize","actor":"support:priyad","session":"s-abc123","role":"support-impersonate","tenant":"<TENANT_REDACTED>","resource":"cluster-prod","result":"ok"}
{"ts":"2026-03-02T09:42:01Z","svc":"auth","evt":"session.expire","session":"s-abc123","reason":"ttl"}
```

Kevin O'Neill: HMAC signing example we'll use:

```bash
# create signature for the whole ndjson file
openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$ACME_VERIF_KEY" -binary sample.ndjson | base64
```

Priya Desai: Add a verification section: include fingerprint of the verification key (sha256 of key), and steps: 1) obtain sample.ndjson and signature.txt, 2) run openssl with provided key to verify.

Daniel Ruiz: For SIEM export flow: we push gzipped ndjson to S3 with enforced server-side encryption (SSE-KMS). We provide a pre-signed staging URL for their SIEM to pull, or we can configure our forwarder to deliver via TLS syslog. I'll document both options.

Maria Chen: KMS wording: "Support sessions never receive raw customer key material. All KMS decrypt/encrypt operations are performed by the platform; support engineers can call proxy endpoints which log the operation, but do not reveal plaintext keys. Customers may choose HSM-backed keys in Private deployments." Priya, can you refine?

Priya Desai: Refining: "KMS proxying: operations authenticated by service identity; logs include truncated key identifiers (sha256 prefix) and operation type. We include proof-of-operation lines in the audit sample (no key material)."

security-bot: Reminder: enterprise audit retention = configurable up to 3 years; default 365 days.

Kevin O'Neill: One more small ask from Acme: show us an automated evidence snippet proving token expired without manual action. We'll include timestamped session.create -> session.expire lines and mention our cron-driven cleanup TTL enforcement.

Daniel Ruiz: I'll add the enforcement entry from the manager service:

```text
2026-03-02T09:42:01Z manager.enforce session=s-abc123 action=expire reason=ttl_enforced
```

Maria Chen: Perfect. Format: short cover email text (plain English), zip of sample.ndjson + signature + verification-instructions.txt + short KMS blurb + RBAC excerpt (one paragraph). Target: ship to Acme security by EOD tomorrow.

Priya Desai: Also flag legal for the HMAC verification key exchange method. We shouldn't transmit verification keys over insecure channels. Use SSO-protected artifact link or out-of-band exchange.

Kevin O'Neill: Noted. I'll prepare package and put artifacts on secure share with ACL to Acme contacts only.

Maria Chen: Thanks team. Ping here if anything blocks. :white_check_mark:
